   STAFF REPORT

 Meeting Date:  June 29, 2026
 To:  2028 Olympics Committee Liaisons Councilmember Friedman
  and Councilmember Nazarian
 From:  Magdalena Davis, Community Outreach Manager
  Matthew Brown, Recreation Services Manager
 Subject:  Planning and discussion for the 2028 Summer Olympic and
  Paralympic Games in Los Angeles
 Attachments:  None

INTRODUCTION
The Los Angeles 2028 Summer Olympics City Council Liaison Committee has been
established with Councilmember Friedman, Councilmember Nazarian, and City staff, to
discuss and guide the evaluation and pursuit of opportunities for programs, events,
partnerships, and visitor amenities, and to help coordinate strategic planning efforts in
advance of the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games in Los Angeles. As the first meeting
in this series dedicated solely and specifically to the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic
Games, staff will be seeking some initial direction on the range of programs, events,
partnerships, and visitor amenities, that Council may be interested in pursuing. These
could include the use of short and long-term rentals of private homes for Olympic
hospitality houses, or events during the Olympic Games hosted by the City for the public,
Olympic committees for an invited guest list or public, or other programs.

To facilitate the ongoing planning process, and continued discussion and direction needed
to implement and coordinate these strategic planning efforts - staff recommend that the
committee begin meeting on a bi-monthly basis, increasing the frequency to monthly
meetings with quarterly reports to City Council as the planning process develops, and
funding needs become clearly identified.

DISCUSSION
As the Host City of the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games, the Greater Los Angeles
area will become the central focal point for events, housing for athletes and delegates,
and community celebrations, with well over five million anticipated domestic and
international visitors to the region, in conjunction with the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic
Games. With the Olympic Games estimated to produce between $13 and $17 billion in
 Meeting Date: June 29, 2026

economic impact within the region, Los Angeles County will play host to both travelers and
local residents attending the Olympic Games and participating and attending programs
and events in support of the games all throughout the region. As a major, internationally
known and iconic tourist destination, Beverly Hills will be a highly sought-after destination
for visitors, locals, and residents during the lead up to, and through the 2028 Olympic and
Paralympic Games. While the majority of the games will not be hosted in, or taking place
within Beverly Hills proper, regions hosting the Olympics typically anticipate that hotels in
highly attractive cities like Beverly Hills will be fully booked, restaurants will see peak
reservation traffic, and corporations, Olympic delegations, and sponsors will seek out
Beverly Hills to host events, celebrations, gatherings, and festivities around the games.

City staff have already received, and begun reviewing, initial prospects for proposed
activations and programs to occur in support, or conjunction with, the Olympic games –
and evaluating any potential amendments, or adjustments, to current city policies and
ordinances that could be considered, and necessary to accommodate certain proposals.
For this first Liaison Committee meeting staff can review initial proposals received thus far
and seek direction from the Liaisons on the kind of programs, events, partnerships, visitor
amenities, and planning principles, to guide planning for, and around, the 2028 Olympic
and Paralympic Games in Los Angeles. Some of the initial topics to discuss, review, and
seek feedback on at today’s meeting are as follows.

1972 Munich Summer Olympics massacre memorial event
Staff received a request through the Israeli Olympic Committee to host a memorial event
remembering the 1972 Munich Summer Olympics massacre and kidnapping of 11 Israeli
Olympic athletes. The event is a cooperative between the Israeli, German, and United
States Olympic Committees, and the request would include the City partnering on the
event as the host venue and sharing of some total costs to be determined. Typically, a
one-day evening event for an invited guest list around the Opening Ceremony, the event
has had approximately 400 attendees in the past, including heads of state. The 2028 date
for this event is to be determined, and both City Hall and the Wallis have been considered
as potential venues. For security purposes, the overall details of the event may be
presented to Liaisons and Council, with the particulars discussed in Closed Session or
administratively. Staff request direction from the Liaisons to understand the City’s interest
in being the partner host for the venue of this event.

Short-term/Long-term rentals and usage of private homes
Staff have received requests from countries and entities interested in the usage of private
homes for long-term rentals to serve as Olympic hospitality houses, from Romania, or for
the use of existing country homes for events, such as the French Consulate house, as
well as abundant interest in the usage of long-term and short-term rentals for visitors
around the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. Community Development is planning to
bring a Study Session item to City Council at some point during the summer of 2026, to
receive direction on this item, and the subsequent adjustments needed to our current
code.

Policy and ordinance amendments
The City’s current banner policy and anti-advertising ordinance do not allow for street pole
banner designs that are not co-branded with the City shield, and only make exceptions in
individual City leases, such as the banners at the Wallis. In order to consider having the

official LA28 Olympic and Paralympic banners, the banner policy and advertising
ordinance would require temporary modifications.
Liaisons may also want to consider any other policy adjustments to allow for official LA28
items in our gardens, parks, or other public right of way, either by modifying current code
or administratively on a case-by-case basis, by establishing qualifications for
consideration.

Future agenda items
Liaisons may provide direction on future agenda items for staff to research and develop,
including participation in the Cultural Olympiad led by LA County, along with neighboring
and participating cities, that could include public events and programs such as watch party
locations, or events to host countries that contain our Sister Cities: Herzliya, Israel;
Cannes, France; Acapulco, Mexico; Pudong, China, and future friendship cities. These
programs could be developed as new events, rekindling of prior partnerships, or by
adjusting regular summer programming to include and incorporate Olympic and
Paralympic activities or themes.

FISCAL IMPACT
Funding will be required as certain proposals move from the discussion phase to seeking
approval for implementation, or to move forward with actions or stages that will require
funding. Staff anticipate increasing the frequency of the 2028 Olympics Committee Liaison
meetings as planning develops and bringing items from the Liaison Committee to City
Council on a quarterly basis, with funding needs as they arise for Council to provide
direction on any fiscal impacts.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff are seeking discussion and direction from the Liaison Committee on the initial
proposals received thus far, and seeking direction on the range of programs, events,
partnerships, and visitor amenities that the Liaisons may be interested in pursuing for the
2028 Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games in Los Angeles.

  Keith Sterling,
  Deputy City Manager
